newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian PM maintains backing for new finmin.
newsitem.headline: Latvian PM maintains backing for new finmin.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele is sure over his backing for a new finance minister although the minister is being investigated for a conflict of interests.
Shkele on Monday backed the choice of the largest government party, the Democratic Party Saimnieks, of Vassili Melnik as new finance minister after the previous one was sacked in October.
But the prosecutor's office confirmed newspaper reports that Melnik is being investigated for a conflict of interests.
Newspaper Diena said Melnik, 29, was being investigated as he was a board member of the port of Riga and chairman of the Riga Shipyard company and its shareholder at the same time.
"Prime Minister Shkele has no reason not to trust the decision of the biggest parliamentary party," Shkele's spokesman Jurgis Lepnieks told Reuters.
He said that any candidate put forward by a party was the responsibility of that party.

Melniks, 29, is a businessman who is head of several companies, including a ship repair company, a board member at Latvian Gas and the deputy chairman of the board of the Latvian Shipping Company, one of the Baltic state's largest firms.
